usage.s01: ## How the app uses this data
usage.s02Anchors: Knowledge: entries stand in “Entries” (table, tree, structure, matrix, canvas — by views), each with its own page (fields, references, learning order); kinds, templates, views and ways of adding — in “Schemas”; entry points ("anchors") add a button “In Knowledge” next to the work in the Library and in the reader.
usage.s03: Learning: templates turn entries into cards (with the key “template:entry”); revisions choose from the cards and ask; “Path” shows the learning order; views and revisions with a “Knowness filter” show what the learner is ready for.
usage.s04Landscape: Landscape (view "landscape", on a page "krajobraz"): from the learning order and knowness it computes a height for each entry (valley, ring, mountains), from the view’s grouping — the direction; there the learner chooses what to learn, sets a goal (saved privately like progress), and the lock asks to first revise weak cards on the way before the entry.
usage.s05About: Reading in Learning: before the first question about an entry from "about" comes “New topic” (title and lead, “Read more”, “Read text” to the place in the source), after the answer — the explanation; both according to its kind’s "reading", and without it — the summary or the first paragraph, then the text fields.
usage.s06: Answers: each is saved encrypted in the browser — for the learner and for the course’s intake area (Settings), where the teacher sees “Progress”; the knowness of cards and entries is computed from them. The service does not read answers; it only sees when the next revision is due and how many cards are waiting — per person and base (for reminders).
usage.s07: Pages: the modules “View” (table, tree, matrix, map), “Revision”, “Course / story”, “Entry card” read the base as the page’s reader sees it; the page’s person learns (signed in — they themselves, without an account — this browser).
usage.s08Rewards: Rewards ("rewards"): the modules “Points and streak” and “Live statistics” on a page and Learning (Motivation “Points and rewards”, tab “Rewards”) compute points, streak, daily goal, level and badges from the answers — live, with every answer; none of this is stored.
usage.s09: Other knowledge bases that use this one as a source see its kinds, entries, templates, revisions and flows read-only; the AI link and MCP read it unchanged.
usage.s10:
Other worlds ("@@name:…"): on the page of an entry and topic there is “In other worlds” — cards with the name of that base, one sentence and the learner’s state THERE; a link in the text opens such a card; a detour into another world plays that story with the bar “Physics › Newton’s laws › History: Glorious Revolution” and returns to its step; in the landscape a portal mark next to the field (close up) and a list in the topic panel — no lines between bases.
    Only those who can read that base see them (others see nothing; the owner sees “unavailable”); progress is saved in the base where it happens (answers in History belong to History); they do not affect the knowness, landscape, goals or revisions of this base.
    Broken ones (that entry deleted, name unknown) are hidden from learners, and the owner sees them in “To do”; when deleting an entry, the preview says which bases link to it.
usage.s11: Who reads: whoever reads its area (in a public area — everyone); entries are encrypted with the area key.
usage.s12Remove: The import deletes only what the document lists with "remove": true (the preview shows each), and does not touch answers or progress: a new card starts without history, and a card whose correct answer changed starts its history again (changing the "tests" weights does not change the history).

rewards.s01Rewards: "rewards" — rewards (points, day streak, daily goal, levels, badges); several per base, each place chooses its own (module “Points and streak” / “Live statistics” on a page, Settings → Motivation → “Points and rewards” in Learning):
rewards.s02Ref:
{"ref": "@kurs/punkty", "name": "Points and streak",
   "points": {"correct": 10, "partial": 5, "wrong": 1, "first": 5, "known": 20, "fast": 0, "combo": 15, "goal": 50, "streak": 5},
   "known": {"days": 1}, "fast": {"seconds": 8}, "combo": {"every": 5}, "goal": {"amount": 20, "unit": "cards|answers|points|minutes"},
   "streak": {"counts": "goal|any", "grace": 0, "max": 10},
   "levels": [{"at": 0, "name": "Beginner"}, {"at": 100, "name": "Student"}],
   "badges": [{"id": "tydzien", "name": "A week in a row", "icon": "star|flame|target|book|bolt|crown|medal|leaf|check|rocket", "measure": "points|streak|best|known|cards|answers|correct|days|combo|goals|level|regions|map|clean", "atLeast": 7, "points": 0, "says": "…", "kind": "start|consistency|accuracy|volume|goals|exploration", "tier": 2}]}
rewards.s03Points: "points": "correct" × correctness for a correct answer (from 90%), "partial" × correctness for a partly correct one, "wrong" for a wrong one (for trying), "first" for the first answer to a card, "known" for a consolidated card (next revision at least "known.days" days away), "fast" for a correct one within "fast.seconds" s, "combo" every "combo.every" correct in a row (a break over 30 min starts again), "goal" for the daily goal, "streak" × day of the streak (up to "streak.max")
rewards.s04Goal: "goal": the daily goal — "cards" different cards, "answers" answers, "points" points (without bonuses for goal and streak), "minutes" minutes of learning; "streak": a streak day is a day with the goal ("goal") or with any learning ("any"), "grace" — this many days of break do not break the streak
rewards.s05Badges: "badges": "regions" (map regions fully known), "map" (percentage of map topics, 0–100) and "clean" (days in a row without overdue cards) are computed by the landscape — such a badge arrives when the learner opens it, and its date is saved in their progress; "kind" (optional) is the category on the page “Badges and levels” — without it, it follows from the measure; badges of one category with the same measure are the steps of one ladder: from the lowest threshold wood, bronze, silver, gold, diamond (a ladder of up to 5 steps: one each; a longer one spreads the five materials evenly, with a number within the material — “Silver II”), "tier" 1–5 (optional) sets the material directly; the built-in rules have 5 categories of 12 steps each, roughly exponential (the first easy, the highest after months), and 12 levels, each roughly twice as far
rewards.s06: points are not stored: the app computes them from the learner’s answers — changing the rules changes everyone’s points; whatever is missing is taken from the built-in rules; there are no rankings (only in live sessions)

anchors.s01Anchors: "anchors" — entry points from the Library: {"ref", "name", "work": "@work key or identifier", "locator": "p. 45–60" | "p. 1–3; 27–30" | "I q. 2 a. 3; a. 4" | "" (whole work), "entry": "@entry of this base (not a work)", "view": "@view or its name", "note"}
anchors.s02: next to the work in the Library a button with the entry point’s name appears — only for those who can read this base (the Library saves nothing); several entry points of one work may concern the whole, the beginning, the end, also several parts at once
anchors.s03: parts are separated by “;”; a part that starts at a lower level than the previous one belongs to its frame (“I q. 2 a. 3; a. 4” — article 4 of the same question; “vol. 2, ch. 1; ch. 9” — chapter 9 of the same volume)

main.s03Quote: a template may concern a kind from the library ("quote", "work", "person") or from the Scriptorium ("text", "delivery", "project") that this base uses: then the cards come from their entries, e.g. {"name": "Place of the quote", "kinds": ["quote"], "direction": "locator", "graph": …}
main.s06Random: computing nodes: "random" ({"min", "max", "step"} or {"list": ["3", "5"]}, or a list from the input "items"; "count": 4 — this many DIFFERENT at once) — draws for every card; "calc" (“Compute”): {"expr": "p0 * p1; p0 + 1", "inputs": 2, "decimals": 2} — expressions in the drawing language (mod, round, fmt, sqrt …), one per line or after “;”, each gives a value (a list — several); p0…p7 — the first number from the input, n0…n7 — how many values came, l0…l7 — all input values as a list (entries as records: sum(l0, it.masa)); "aggregate" (“Collect”): {"op": "sum"|"count"|"min"|"max"|"avg", "decimals"} — input "values" (e.g. "follow" → numeric "field"); the output "value" connects to "pattern", "answer.number" ("expected") and "answer.one" ("expected" or "distractors", e.g. "p0 + 1; p0 - 1; p0 * 2")
main.s08Card: node "card" also takes "hints" (hints — texts, from gentle to specific) and "solution" (the solution — a text with the task’s values, after the answer)
main.s09: Knowness — computed by the app, the same everywhere (it is not set in JSON):
main.s10: every answer is saved; a card remembers only a few values: when it was last answered, how much time really passed before that answer, the interval until next time and the best interval before the last mistake;
main.s11:
right (from 90%): interval = the time that really passed × 3 (answering before the due date does not shorten it); partly: a third of that time, at least a day if days have passed; wrong (below 25%): 5 minutes; right just after a mistake: 0.4 × the best interval before the mistake
    — e.g. wrong after 5 days: comes back after 5 minutes; right right after: in 2 days; right again after 2 days: in 6 days;
main.s12: card knowness: correctness of the last answer × √(10 ÷ (1 + 9 · time since the answer ÷ interval)) — right after a correct one 3.16, on the revision day 1, then it falls more and more slowly (10 % only after 111 intervals, never 0); after a wrong one 0;
main.s13: three bands (fixed): “known” from 1 (100 %) — not time yet; “due” from 0.1 to 1 — you know it, and now (or soon) it needs revising: a due date does NOT mean “I don’t know”; “unknown” below 0.1 — never asked, recently wrong or forgotten (111 intervals past due);
main.s14Weight: entry knowness: the average knowness of its cards WITH AN ANSWER, weighted by "weight" from "tests" (a card not yet asked is no evidence); what builds on it (fields with "prerequisite" — half — and dependencies from Settings, with their weight) raises it at least to that share of the best of them — never to their sum
main.s16EndWhenDone:
LESSON — an ordinary revision with "endWhenDone": true, "pick": "next", "order": "general": during it a bar “x of y cards”, at the end a summary (done, right the first time, time, cards with a wrong answer and “Practise these again”);
    "next": "@kurs/lekcja-2" — the lasting name (or identifier) of the revision that comes after this one: at the end a button “Next lesson”
main.s17Type: also steps shared with views: {"type": "follow", "config": {"field": "authors", "back": false}} — cards of the entries the reference leads to (or, "back": true, that point to these entries); {"type": "filter.rule", "config": {"rule": {"op": "and", "items": [{"field", "cmp", "value"}]}}} — cards of entries meeting the rule; {"type": "structure", "config": {"dir": "down|up", "one": true}} — cards of entries that lie in the structure under these entries (or above them); "follow" and "structure" with "keep": true also keep the cards they started from
main.s18Type: source “kind from the library”: {"type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "quote", "from": "<library identifier>"}} — "from" empty: from this base and all sources
main.s19Type:
source “view”: {"type": "source.view", "config": {"view": "@widok"}} — cards of the entries a saved view shows: the view decides what is in play, the revision chooses from it; changing the view changes the revision, and its “Knowness filters” at the end work during the revision
    e.g. {"name": "From general to specific", "graph": {"nodes": [{"id": "w", "type": "source.view", "config": {"view": "@fakty/w-ogolne"}}, {"id": "p", "type": "strategy", "config": {"mode": "temporal", "order": "general"}}], "edges": [{"id": "e1", "from": "w", "out": "cards", "to": "p", "in": "cards"}]}}
main.s21Type: “Follow the learning order”: {"type": "learning", "config": {"dir": "before" | "after", "one": true, "keep": true}} — cards of what must be known earlier (or, "after", what builds on it), down to the basics or ("one") one step; "keep": true adds them to the starting cards
main.s22Type: “Sample from each topic”: {"type": "sample", "config": {"perTopic": 2}} — from each topic (the first of the card’s "about", otherwise its entry) up to "perTopic" random cards stay; a different sample every day; together with “Together” ("union") e.g. all gap cards + a sample of the rest — a spot check
main.s23Strategy:
“Way of asking” ("strategy"): {"mode": "temporal" (by what I know) | "levels" | "once" | "random", "order", "pick", "perTopic", "stackSize", "count", "levels", "minCorrectness", "endWhenDone", "rule"}
    "once" (“Whole stack, each once”): every card of the stack exactly once, in "order"; a wrong answer does NOT come back in this run; a card whose condition starts to hold during it joins the queue; at the end each topic as “you know it” or “gap” (gap: one of its cards was not fully right) with “Topic”, “See in the story” and “Fill the gaps” — this is how “Check what you know” works
    "random": like "once", but only the first "count" cards (default 20) by "order" (without "order": random)
    "levels" (“Levels”): a stack of "stackSize" cards; a right answer raises the card one level (up to "levels", default 5, 1–20), a wrong one goes back to level 1, and a right one after a wrong one also goes to 1; a card at the highest level does not come back in this run — the run ends by itself
    "minCorrectness" (0–1, default 1) — from which correctness an answer counts as right (for the stack and levels); "stackSize" (default 20) — how many cards at once in the stack ("temporal", "levels"); "rule" — what the revision changes in the strictness of the template’s checking, e.g. {"caseSensitive": false}
    "temporal": a stack of "stackSize" cards; a card leaves the stack only after a fully right answer ("minCorrectness", default 1); a free place takes first what is due (weakest first), then unknown ones (new, recently wrong, forgotten — in "order"), and when there are neither — known ones that are known least (“in reserve”: the revision does not end by itself); "endWhenDone": true — the end when nothing is waiting and there is nothing new
    "order" — order: "general" (general first — by levels of the learning order) | "text" (as in the source text — place in the work) | "date" (by the earliest date of the entry) | "random" | "given" (as they come) | "due" (overdue first); without "order": "general" in a stack, "random" in a fixed queue
    "pick" — the choice from the stack: "next" (strictly the next by order) | "weighted" (random, more often what is known less and has waited longer; default) | "sample" (a sample: from each topic only "perTopic" random cards, default 2 — e.g. "mode": "once", "pick": "sample", "perTopic": 2 spot-checks every topic; then strictly the next); another value — the import warns, works like the default; at every card the learner sees why it came
main.s24Name: “Check what you know — the whole book”: {"name": "Check what you know — the whole book", "graph": {"nodes": [{"id": "q", "type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "question"}}, {"id": "k", "type": "filter.rule", "config": {"rule": {"op": "and", "items": [{"field": "core", "cmp": "eq", "value": "true"}]}}}, {"id": "p", "type": "strategy", "config": {"mode": "once", "order": "general", "pick": "next"}}], "edges": [{"id": "e1", "from": "q", "out": "cards", "to": "k", "in": "cards"}, {"id": "e2", "from": "k", "out": "cards", "to": "p", "in": "cards"}]}} — every key question once (without a ready-made revision: the button “Check what you know” above the landscape does the same for the region in view)
main.s25Type: “Fill the gaps”: source → {"type": "filter.when", "config": {"when": {"type": "knowness", "rel": "core", "each": "any", "band": "unknown"}}} → “Together” ← (the same source → {"type": "sample", "config": {"perTopic": 1}}) → “Way of asking” {"mode": "once"}: all gap cards and one spot check each from the rest ("band": "unknown" also covers never-asked ones — first “Check what you know”)
main.s26Type: “Basics first” is ordinary steps: {"type": "learning", "config": {"dir": "before", "keep": true}} → {"type": "filter.when", "config": {"when": {"type": "knowness", "rel": "before", "band": "learned"}}} → “Way of asking” with "order": "general"; the old step "gate" is converted to them by import and export
main.s28Graph: "graph": {"nodes": [{"id", "type", "x", "y", "config"}], "edges": [{"id", "from", "out", "to", "in": "in"}]} — steps and transitions ("out" — the step’s output); "start": id of the first step (omitted — the only step nothing leads to);
main.s29End: THE PATH MUST BE LOGICAL: exactly one beginning and one end (a step "end", "return" or "handoff"), every step reachable from the beginning, from every step the end can be reached, every output ("right" AND "wrong" of a question, every choice option) leads to a step; the import preview names every step that breaks this (a second beginning, an unreachable step, a dead end, a loop without exit), and a flow without a beginning or without an end is not saved;
main.s31Goals: "goals": [{"id", "title", "condition"}] — goals (a flow with goals is a task); reached ones are saved with the learner’s place and stay reached; a flow with goals lets its unit sink into the valley only when it is completed AND every goal is reached (without goals: when completed);
main.s32Id: REVIEW IN ONE STEP (since 2026-11-05 — instead of several steps per question): {"id": "przeglad", "type": "review", "config": {"of": "story", "threshold": 0.9}} → "passed" | "notyet"; asks again the questions of THIS flow ("question" steps; "of": "@other-flow" — its questions) that the learner does not know yet — each once per round (wrong ones do not come back in this round; known ones are skipped as always), then shows the result (“You know 9 of 10 (90 %)”): at least "threshold" (0–1, default 0.9) → "passed", otherwise "notyet" (unconnected: the story ends with the review not yet passed, and at the end stands “Repeat the review”; or connect it to a choice “Try again” / “Stop for now” — not to itself); stores the value "value" (default “<story name without @>.przeglad”: 1 passed, 0 not); a flow WITHOUT "goals" gets the goal “Review passed” by itself ("goal" — another name for the goal, e.g. “Durchsicht bestanden”) with the condition on this value, and “Repeat the review” returns to this step (unless "review" points elsewhere); on the path it is one node “Review”; example: {"nodes": [… {"id": "q9", "type": "question", "config": {"of": "@kurs/q/opady"}}, {"id": "przeglad", "type": "review", "config": {"of": "story", "threshold": 0.9, "goal": "Review passed"}}, {"id": "koniec", "type": "end"}], "edges": [… {"from": "q9", "out": "right", "to": "przeglad"}, {"from": "q9", "out": "wrong", "to": "przeglad"}, {"from": "przeglad", "out": "passed", "to": "koniec"}]} ("notyet" unconnected)
main.s33DeszczPrzeglad:
REVIEW FROM SEPARATE STEPS (the old way, still works) AT THE END OF A STORY (in the same flow, the same questions as in the story — the same card history, never copies): a counter with the story’s name at the start ("deszcz.przeglad" — values belong to the learner, not to one story); a "set" step resets it at the start of the review, and "review": "<id of this step>" says where “Repeat the review” leads (without "review": to the beginning); each question "right" → step "set" {"actions": [{"type": "add", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "by": 1}]} → next question, "wrong" → straight to the next question; at the end "condition" {"type": "value", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "op": "ge", "than": 3} — "yes" → end, "no" → back to the start of the review (or to a choice “Try again” / “Stop for now”: a story finished without a passed review stays on the plain as “review not yet passed”); a goal with THE SAME condition: "goals": [{"id": "przeglad", "title": "Review passed", "condition": {"type": "value", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "op": "ge", "than": 3}}]
    {"ref": "@kurs/deszcz", "name": "Where rain comes from", "look": "dialogue", "unit": "@kurs/lekcja/deszcz", "review": "p0", "goals": [{"id": "przeglad", "title": "Review passed", "condition": {"type": "value", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "op": "ge", "than": 3}}],
     "graph": {"nodes": [{"id": "p0", "type": "set", "config": {"actions": [{"type": "set", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "to": 0}]}}, {"id": "p1", "type": "question", "config": {"of": "@kurs/q/parowanie"}}, {"id": "p1ok", "type": "set", "config": {"actions": [{"type": "add", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "by": 1}]}}, …, {"id": "pz", "type": "condition", "config": {"condition": {"type": "value", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "op": "ge", "than": 3}}}, {"id": "koniec", "type": "end"}],
      "edges": [{"from": "p0", "out": "next", "to": "p1"}, {"from": "p1", "out": "right", "to": "p1ok"}, {"from": "p1", "out": "wrong", "to": "p2"}, {"from": "p1ok", "out": "next", "to": "p2"}, …, {"from": "pz", "out": "yes", "to": "koniec"}, {"from": "pz", "out": "no", "to": "p0"}]}}
main.s34About: QUESTIONS ABOUT TOPICS, NEVER ABOUT THE UNIT: the "about" of a story’s questions lists topics; the unit ("unit") has no cards of its own — otherwise it would sink after a few right answers without the story, and its button would practise cards instead of playing the story;
main.s35Narrators: "narrators" — who narrates, depending on values: [{"character": "@piotr", "condition": {"type": "value", "value": "przewodnik", "op": "eq", "than": 1}}, {"character": "@maria"}] — the first whose condition holds narrates (without a condition: always); their portrait and name stand above the step and introduce its title
main.s36Unit: "unit": "@wpis" — the UNIT this story is: one field in the landscape (also when it has no cards itself), “Show path” shows the story’s path, and when the story is finished (with goals: and the review passed), the field sinks into the valley; a reference field of the unit with "prerequisite": "up" (e.g. “Requires” → topics) locks the story until you know that — in the landscape it stands as a mountain with a road to it
main.s37Path: the story button (a field in the landscape, a node in Learning → Path and in the module "path"): “Start the story” (new), “Continue the story” (on the way — from where they stopped), “Repeat the review” (completed, goal not reached — from "review"), “Open the story” (passed); it never practises the unit’s cards
main.s38: the locked screen (the player before a story, the same logic as the landscape): something is missing before the unit — a list from the basics with links and “Learn” at each, plus “Set as goal” (a goal in the landscape); everything learned, but there are weak cards in the chain — “Revise first (N)” with exactly those cards, then straight into the story; whoever writes in the base has “Preview anyway”
main.s39Name: a flow from a presentation (ONE story = presentation page + this flow, no copies): {"name": "The way", "look": "scenes", "presentation": "parafia/droga", "unit": "@lekcja", "narrators": […]} — without its own "graph": its map is the page’s storyboard (scenes, buttons, questions, gates, values — "story" in the page JSON, with "base": id of this base); in Learning it plays that presentation, and answers, values and the place where someone stopped count in this base (the same place as on the page); only those who can see the page see it; a question on a scene with "question": "@pytanie" counts like a "question" step here, and the scene’s "about" says what the scene is about (for the path); a review on the page: a value in "story.values", "set" gates (zero, +1 on "right") and a "condition" gate with the result, "review": "<key of the scene where the review starts>", the flow’s "goals" as above (counted from the page’s values); the page opens at the scene from the address "?scena=<klucz>"
main.s40Type: the learner’s place (private, like progress; never in an export or in MCP): step, visited, walked chapter paths, “completed” (end reached — stays also after “from the beginning”), reached goals — the condition {"type": "flow", "flow": "@przebieg", "state": "done" | "started" | "goal", "goal": "goal id"} reads them in views ("filter.when"), revisions and steps of a landscape view (e.g. topics only after a completed story)
main.s41Show: the path next to a story (2026-11-04): a map of the flow’s PARTS, computed from the graph alone — beginning and end as their own marks; “slides to read” (consecutive steps "show"/"line"/"expand"/"opening"/scene without questions), “questions to answer” (consecutive "question"/scene with questions; a step with both — both counters), “review” (a loop returning to the questions until you know them all, and a step with "review"; a single slide right before it belongs to it), “choice of path” ("choice", "chapters" and a scene with several buttons — drawn as a fork with the counter “choose 1 of 3” / “chosen 1 of 3” / “completed 2 of 3 paths”); "condition"/"set" steps are transparent; always from the bottom (beginning) to the top (end), all in a frame (scaled down; “+”, “−”, “Fit”, “Full screen”), the current part larger, outlined and with its name beside it, other names on pointing (first touch — a popup, second — opens), the legend always under the map; “X of Y” counts exactly the hexagons drawn; a part is completed when walked (questions: and learned, review: and everything known); old description: a small path map follows the step; a pointed choice option highlights its path; a click on a free step moves the story to it; on a page it also stands separately as the module "path" ({"library", "flow": "<flow id>"} — also for a flow from a presentation)
main.s42RecreatioCogitaFlow: "recreatio.cogita.flow" — ONE flow together with what it shows (export from the flow editor): {"format": "recreatio.cogita.flow", "version": 1, "flow": {flow as above}, "entities": [the entries it shows — also characters and the unit "unit"]} — imported in the same place as a course; entries with "ref" merge with existing ones
main.s44Views: "views" — views (the same steps as a revision, over entries): {"name", "mode": "table|tree|matrix|map|canvas|outline|quilt|landscape", "steps": [step, …], "query", "group", "matrix", "columns": ["field key" | "#axis:@axis"], "sort": {"key", "dir": 1|-1}, "landscape": {"nest": "field"}}
main.s45SourceAll: sources at the start — several in a row add up (e.g. sermons and comments): "source.all" | "source.kind" {"kind": "@rodzaj" or "text" from the Scriptorium, "from"} | "source.collection" {"collection": "@zbiór"} | "source.list" {"ids": ["@wpis"]};
main.s46SourceFrom: also "source.from" {"entry": "@kazanie"} — what an entry points to (a sermon: its quotes, statements, dictionary words, places from the plan; in a revision: “From entry” — a revision from the sermon);
main.s47Follow: then "follow" {"field", "back"}, "structure" {"dir": "down|up", "one": true} (along the structure fields — without "one": to the very end; "one": true — one level) and "filter.rule" {"rule"} (a source after another step starts anew);
main.s48FilterWhen:
also "filter.when" {"when": condition} and "learning" {"dir", "one", "keep"} — the same as in a revision; in a view the knowness of whoever is looking counts (the learner on this account; on a page — the page’s person or this browser),
    e.g. facts of a period only once the period is known: {"type": "filter.when", "config": {"when": {"type": "knowness", "rel": "okres", "op": "ge", "than": 1}}}; only entries whose basics are known: "rel": "before";
main.s49Sort: columns and "sort" from knowness: "#knowness" (knowness of the entry), "#due" (when to revise), "#level" (level in the learning order), e.g. "sort": {"key": "#knowness", "dir": 1} — weakest first;
main.s50Mode: "mode": "quilt" (Progress map) — a tile per entry in the colour of how well the learner knows it (new, learning, due, known), grouped like "group" (e.g. ideas by lesson under chapters: {"by": "axis", "kind": "@lekcja", "via": ["lekcja"], "sort": {"field": "nr"}, "group": "rozdzial"}); click: text, questions, “Practise this”, “Open in source”; visible in Learning → Progress (also to the teacher) and in the module “View”
main.s51World: "landscape": {"style": "world"} — the WORLD MAP instead of hexagons: topics (places) as round pillars, stories (flows) as railway lines between them, branchings as interchange stations, the unit's "Requires", the condition of a choice option and a "condition" step as tickets of sections; pillar height = cards still missing; the app computes positions (never in an import); conquest levels in the settings: {"settings": {"levelsSetup": {"levels": 0–5, "rules": [{"pct", "attempts": "any|one|first"}], "knownShare", "pillarWidth", "locked"}}} (default 0 — nothing changes); blocks with parts through a field with "part" — guide "guide-world-map";
main.s52Mode:
"mode": "outline" (Structure) draws the sources as roots, and under them what the steps lead to; "outline": {"chip": "field key above each step (e.g. role)", "order": "tree|text" (without "order": the reader’s last choice, and initially text order for Thomas and a tree in other works), "by": "field key by which the steps of one level are arranged first (e.g. time — story time; without "by": by place in the work)", "tie": "field key at the same place (e.g. nr)"};
    a view opened from an entry (an entry point from the Library) replaces everything before the first “Follow…” with this entry; e.g. {"name": "Argument", "mode": "outline", "steps": [{"type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "@krok"}}, {"type": "filter.rule", "config": {"rule": {"op": "and", "items": [{"field": "nalezy", "cmp": "empty"}]}}}, {"type": "structure", "config": {"dir": "down"}}], "outline": {"chip": "rola", "order": "tree", "tie": "nr"}}
main.s53Group:
grouping (tree "group", rows and columns "matrix": {"rows": grouping, "cols": grouping}): {"by": "kind"} | {"by": "field", "field": "key"} | {"by": "axis", "kind": "@rodzaj", "via", "through", "depth", "sort", "group"} — AXIS: its values are entries of a kind
    "via": ["pole"] — through which reference fields an entry belongs to a value (empty: through any); "through": "pole" or "*" — also one step further (entry → through this field → another entry → through "via" → value); "depth": "all" or a number — "through" across all (or n) levels: on each way up the value of the nearest entry that has one, and an entry with its own value has only that (e.g. {"by": "axis", "kind": "@obszar", "via": ["obszar"], "through": "wymaga", "depth": "all", "sort": {"field": "nr"}}; in the landscape an upward structure field works the same without "depth")
    "sort": {"field": "numer"} — order by a numeric field of the value, or {"list": "@rozaniec", "field": "tajemnice"} — by the order in a reference field of another entry; without "sort" — by name
    "group": "czesc" — headings: a reference field of the value (e.g. part of the mysteries); in a matrix above the columns and between the rows
main.s54: column "#axis:@rodzaj" — the values of this axis (entries of the kind) the entry points to
main.s56Name:
e.g. a 20 × 12 matrix — Mystery × Area: {"name": "Mystery × Area", "mode": "matrix", "steps": [{"type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "text"}}, {"type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "@komentarz"}}], "matrix": {"rows": {"by": "axis", "kind": "@tajemnica", "sort": {"field": "numer"}, "group": "czesc"}, "cols": {"by": "axis", "kind": "@obszar", "group": "grupa"}}}
    — 20 mysteries of the rosary (in four parts) × 12 Marian areas (in groups); in a cell: sermons from the Scriptorium (text kind “Marian sermon” with fields "tajemnica" and "obszar") and comments whose "about" points to the mystery and the area; empty cells are visible too
main.s57View: on a page: module "view" {"library": "<base id>", "view": "<view id>", "mode": "tabela|drzewo|macierz|mapa|postepy|krajobraz", "answers": "<course area id>", "rewards": "<rewards id>"} — a matrix cell (click) and an entry open below, the path in the address separately for each module; in the landscape the page’s person learns: "answers" and "rewards" as in the module “Revision”, learning counts for the modules “Points and streak” and “Live statistics” of this page

entities.s04Blocks:
statement — an entry of a kind with a "blocks" field, e.g. a comment from templates/cogita/komentarz.json:
    "kinds": ["Komentarz"], "data": {"about": [{"value": "@bt", "locator": "Łk 1,35"}], "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Holy Spirit descends on Mary as on the Apostles. Luke describes both events with the same words."}, {"type": "table", "columns": ["Annunciation", "Pentecost"], "rows": [[[{"ref": "@bt", "locator": "Łk 1,35"}], [{"ref": "@bt", "locator": "Dz 1,8"}]]]}]}
    the kind “knowledge” ("knowledge") no longer exists — old entries of it stand in Knowledge under “Old entries”
    there are no topics or perspectives — order comes from your own kinds (e.g. "Mystery" with fields "numer" and "czesc" → kind "Part"; "Area" with a field "grupa"), and entries point to them with reference fields (comment: "about"; sermon: fields of its text kind, e.g. "tajemnica", "obszar")
    a text kind from a Scriptorium the base uses is a kind here: the text has its fields next to the fixed ones (title, date, plan…) — views group and matrices arrange texts by them
    cards from statements: a template with "kinds": ["@kind with a blocks field"] and nodes "statement.thesis" (thesis), "statement.part" ({"n": 2} — the second piece; empty: paragraphs), "statement.table" ({"table": 1, "left": 1, "right": 2} — pairs from columns), "statement.subjects" (about what: values of reference fields, with place)
    text markup in a paragraph and in "markup" fields (the same as in the Scriptorium): paragraphs are separated by an empty line, "## subheading", **bold**, *italic*, [description](https://…), ^[footnote], "> quote", "- item";
    [[word|@wpis]] — a link to an entry (of this base, another base or the library) with these words; never a footnote;
    [@dzielo, p. 23] — source: a work, quote or person from the library becomes a footnote; the same markup pointing to a statement, entry or text gives a link “(see label)” in the text
    QUOTE — a separate paragraph, every line starting with "> "; words in quotation marks, the source as a footnote at the end of the words; the last line starting with "> — " is the attribution (who speaks) under the quote:
      "> “All the following years were deeply marked by this dream.” [@bosco-biografia, p. 5]\n> — Teresio Bosco"
      — shown as a highlighted block with attribution; NEVER “**Quote (T. Bosco):** “…”” in an ordinary paragraph (then it is plain text); footnotes collect themselves under the text — do not write them by hand or a “Footnotes” list
    EXPANDABLE BLOCK (long proof, details): in markup "::: details Beweisidee" on its own line, then the content (paragraphs, formulas, lists), at the end ":::" on its own line — shown collapsed, with this heading; in a "blocks" field also as a block {"type": "details", "summary": "Beweisidee", "text": "content markup"} (saved as a paragraph with this markup)

head.s03: "{courseFormat}" — the whole course: kinds, entries, card templates, revisions, flows, collections, looks, rules, values
head.s06: "{flowFormat}" — a flow together with what it shows
head.s09Ref: "ref" — the entry’s own name, e.g. "@dawid"; other fields refer to it the same way: "@dawid".
head.s10Pole: Existing entries are recognised by identifier (from an export) or by lasting name; the import COMPLETES them in place: fields the document does not mention stay, and "field": null removes a field; a list field given in the document replaces the whole previous list. Before saving, every change to what already exists must be accepted (and can be corrected).
head.s11Ref: CHANGE BY IDENTIFIER: {"ref": "<identyfikator>", "data": {"nazwa": "New name"}} — "kinds" may be omitted (the entry keeps its kinds); "id" works the same as "ref".
head.s12Ref:
DELETING: {"ref": "<identifier or @lasting/name>", "remove": true} — in "entities" (an entry) and in the document lists ("flows", "views", "revisions", "templates", "collections", "forms", "anchors", "looks", "rules", "values", "rewards"); the import does not delete kinds (Schemas → “Delete kind”).
    The preview lists every deletion by name with what points to it; each can be unchecked; nothing disappears silently.
    References to the deleted entry in reference fields of other entries (e.g. "wymaga", "pole", a question’s "about") and in collections are removed from them in the same save — the preview says from which. If something else points to it (a step or the "unit" of a flow, a view, a revision, a template, an entry point, a statement cell), the save fails: fix it in the same document, delete it too, or uncheck the deletion.
    Learners’ answers and history stay: cards of deleted entries simply do not count (progress, statistics, landscape); the entry can be restored from the version history, and then its answers count again.
    The same entry changed and deleted in one document — it is only deleted (with a warning).
head.s13: There is ONE save: new kinds (with lasting names), kind changes, new entries, entry changes, views and the rest, and deletions — all or nothing. The identifiers of new things in the preview are the ones that will be saved.
head.s14: Size: one file up to about 20 MB of JSON (at most 5000 items including deletions; one entry up to 4 MB) — a 4 MB file is one preview and one save (about 6 MB transferred).
head.s15To: The save fails if something would point to a kind or entry that does not exist (e.g. a "to" field with an unknown kind, a value with a nonexistent identifier, a reference to a new thing unchecked in the review) — the list says which item and which field.
head.s16Kinds: A kind can be given by its lasting name ("kinds": ["@wywod/krok"]) — it is found even after it is renamed.
head.s17:
A name with “/” is LASTING: it stays with the entry (also with a view, entry point, template, form, kind), and the same document imported a second time changes the same things instead of creating new ones; letter case does not matter.
    Reconstruction steps: "@<work key>/<rekonstrukcja>/<krok>", e.g. "@kowalski2020/calosc/pytanie", "@kowalski2020/wstep/arg1" — each reconstruction of one work has its own middle part.
    Lasting names are shared by the whole base: a document that hits entry names from another document changes them (the preview says so) — another reconstruction needs another middle part (e.g. "calosc-2").
    Names without “/” work only within their document. Kinds and entries share names, each document kind (views, entry points, templates…) has its own: an entry point "@q" does not change the entry "@q".
    In a reference field and in a cell reference ("ref") a name that leads nowhere is dropped (with a warning naming the entry and field); in a text field "@author/year" is text and stays.
head.s18: A work, person or quote from the library is given by its key or identifier ("@kowalski2020") — only from libraries this base uses (More → Settings → Sources); they are not created here.
head.s20: The export writes lasting names, and the identifiers of its own entries, kinds and documents in views, templates, revisions, flows, collections and forms as "@name" — it can be imported into another base.
head.s21: Who reads: the base is read by whoever reads its area. In a public area (when the base is open: Settings → Who reads) everyone, without an account — the whole base, including question answers and drafts.
head.s22: Single entries are not published: what is to be public goes into a separate base in a public area (entry → Who sees → Move; the identifier stays). Page modules (revision, flow, entry card) read the base as the page’s reader sees it.

usage.s01: ## How the app uses this data
usage.s02: The form appears in Knowledge → “Add” next to the other ways of adding; row by row (or pasted text) it creates entries of its kinds — before saving you see what will be created and what was skipped.
usage.s03: Saved entries are ordinary entries of the base: they appear in “Entries” and in views, and card templates turn them into cards for Learning; new kinds and templates from the document work as if added by hand.
usage.s04: Who sees it: whoever reads the base; whoever can write in it adds. Importing a form does not add any entries by itself.

head.s02: Format: "{schemaFormat}" (the same as the schema), version 1:
head.s04Kinds: "kinds" — the kinds the forms need; without them they must already exist in this knowledge base (recognised by "ref", name or built-in identifier).
head.s05Templates: "templates" — card templates for these kinds (optional): {"ref", "name", "kinds": ["@rodzaj"], "direction", "graph", "tests", "asks"} ("tests" — what their cards check and how strongly, "asks" — which fact they ask about, as in a course).
head.s06Ref: A form with the same "ref" as an existing one changes it in place; a different one creates a new form. Nothing is deleted.
head.s07Ref: "ref" — your own name, e.g. "@miejsce"; within the same document it refers to the kind ("kind": "@miejsce", "to": ["@miejsce"]).

kinds.s02Name: "name" — name, "label" — label pattern, e.g. "{givenNames} {surname}", "tells" — the field that tells namesakes apart,
kinds.s04Builtin:
"builtin" — a change to a built-in kind (person, work, quote — from the library; text, delivery, project — from the Scriptorium; question);
    there is no other built-in content: the base owner writes the kinds or imports a ready-made schema (below)
kinds.s06Structure:
"structure" (reference) — a link in the STRUCTURE (e.g. the argument of an article): "up" — this entry lies UNDER what it points to (step → step above: “Belongs to”); "down" — the entries pointed to lie under it (“Arguments for”);
    the view “Structure” with a "structure" step draws a tree from this in the order of places in the work; such a field does not make a statement an “interpretation”
kinds.s07Part: "part" (reference) — BLOCK WITH PARTS (world map): "up" — the entry is a part of the block it points to; "down" — the block points to its parts; never together with "prerequisite" on the same field (then it counts only as a prerequisite); a part belongs to one block; without such a field there are no blocks — guide "guide-world-map";
kinds.s08External:
"external": true (reference) — the field may also point to entries and stories of ANOTHER knowledge base ("@@historia:@historia/rewolucja-1688", see “OTHER WORLDS” above) — as an offer “In other worlds”, never as a requirement (no "prerequisite" and no "structure"); the editor shows “Link to another world” next to it;
    e.g. {"key": "swiaty", "label": "In other worlds", "type": "ref", "multi": true, "external": true}
kinds.s09When: "when" — a field only for some values of a choice field of the same kind: {"field": "typ", "values": ["bitwa", "traktat"]} — ONE kind with a field “type” instead of a separate kind for each type; the editor shows the field only for these values
kinds.s11Form: a question with a number and quantity: {"form": "number", "prompt": "What torque…?", "answers": ["12"], "unit": "N·m", "quantity": "Torque", "tolerance": 0.1} — “12 N·m” and “0.012 kN·m” are correct, “12 J” is not (energy, although the dimension is the same)
kinds.s14To: "to" (reference) — which kinds it points to: ["@ref of a kind from this document", "Kind name", "work"]; empty — any
kinds.s15Locator:
"locator": true (reference with a place) — each value is {"value": "@dzielo", "locator": "Ps 110"}: a psalm is the Bible from the library + the place, a dictionary entry is the lexicon + “p. 23”; the app reads places in Scripture (Ps 110 · Lk 1:46-55) and searches by them; the text of the Bible is not stored
    e.g. {"key": "miejsce", "label": "Place in Scripture", "type": "ref", "to": ["work"], "locator": true}, and in the entry: "miejsce": {"value": "@bt", "locator": "Ps 110,1-7"}
kinds.s17:
ready-made schemas are files in the repository, imported like any schema (Knowledge → Schemas → Entry kinds → “Schema as JSON” → Import): templates/cogita/komentarz.json (Comment: “About” — references with a place to any entry, “Content” — blocks; with card templates “Thesis” and “Table from content”),
    templates/cogita/slownik.json (Language, Word, Translation, Synonyms, Antonyms — with “Vocabulary” templates), templates/cogita/psalterz.json (psalm with its place in Scripture, breviary places),
    templates/cogita/komentarz-biblijny.json (Comment with arguments for and objections, biblical Comment on a passage of Scripture),
    templates/cogita/pytania.json (one question schema: the built-in kind “Question” with its question types and fields, ways of adding many questions at once — true/false, answer in words, flashcards — and the view “Questions by type”),
    templates/cogita/podstawy.json (learning order: “Concept” with the field “Requires” — "prerequisite": "up" —, “what is it” cards, the view “From the basics” and a way to add concepts with what they require; an atom example to import as a course: templates/cogita/przyklad-atom.json),
    templates/cogita/fakty.json (facts and sources — from any source: a novel about a real person, a textbook, reportage, memoirs, a recording: “Fact” — one claim about the world with a keyword, kind, when, where, about whom, period, source with place, how the source presents it, an assessment after checking (confirmed, disputed, simplified, false, fiction…) and other sources; “Period” — an era or stage with its duration; cards “When?”, “What is known?”, “Is it right?”; views by period, timeline, by assessment and kind, from the basics),
    templates/cogita/zbior.json (a set of items to recognise and tell apart — prefaces and prayers, hymns, psalms, articles of a law, pieces, pictures: “Item” with number, designation, beginning, what it is about, distinguishing marks, image or sound, group, place in works, items easily confused with it and the difference, use; “Group” — a section with what distinguishes it; cards “Which one is it?” by beginning or image, beginnings ↔ designations, “How does it differ?”; views by number, groups, similar items and differences),
    templates/cogita/ksiazka-AI.md (how to prepare any book with AI in two steps: the Library with the full text, then a selection menu — scope, layers, questions, learning order, revisions — and a Cogita course),
    templates/cogita/wywod.json (description of a work: “Argument step” — role (question, thesis, argument, objection… or thread, part of a piece, event, stage, description), place in the work, content, key passage, “Belongs to” — a link in the structure, also in several structures at once, story time; “Stable element” — concept, character, place, motif… in the work or across works (“General”); Comment — one’s own remark; views “Argument” (tree, text order, story time), “Stable elements”; cards with strict checking: passages ↔ theses, thesis for a passage, work of a thesis, meaning of an element; how to prepare the text and structure of a work for AI in two steps: templates/cogita/wywod-AI.md)

forms.s01Forms: "forms" — add forms (they belong to the schema): {"ref", "name", "says", "graph", "keys", "paste", "order"}
forms.s02Pick: node "pick" — a choice made at the start, kept for all rows: "config": {"label", "kinds": ["@rodzaj"], "many", "optional", "value": ["@wpis"]}
forms.s03Entry:
node "entry" — an entry from each row: "config": {"kind": "@rodzaj", "also": ["@inny rodzaj"] (kind chosen for each value; in a list the prefix “Kind name: …”), "label", "many" (several in a row), "optional": true (may stay empty — the entries it leads to are created without it), "reuse": "same|never", "identity": ["pole"],
    "fields": {"pole": {"from": "type|ask|fixed", "value": "text"}}} — type: typed in the row, ask: set at the start ("value" — default), fixed: a fixed value
forms.s04Id:
edge {"id", "from": node, "out": "out", "to": node "entry", "in": key of a reference field} — fills this field with the entry from the node "from";
    several edges to a field that takes several values: values in order by the position of the nodes (top to bottom); an entry is created when all connected values are in the row
forms.s05Order: "order": ["id of an entry node"] — the order of fields in a row (Enter, columns of a pasted list); without it as on the canvas

body.s02Show: pairs: left and right side in the same order; a long list with "show" (2–{showMax}) — that many pairs on a card, each pair has its own card, the ones the learner does not know yet come back
body.s03Show: parts (2026-11-01): every question asks about parts, and each part is a fact counted separately — a pair (match), a statement (many: correctly marked or correctly left out, the result is the average; with "show" each statement has its own card), a word in a gap (gap with several gaps); a question without parts (text, number, date, one, truefalse, flash, order…) has one part, only with "fact" (the fact’s name; "#strona" = that side of the entry from "about", the same fact as a template card with "asks"); "share" (a name) makes questions with the same name share the same parts — one answer counts for every card that asks about it; "truefalse" with "share" is a statement, the same as in "many" with the same "share"
body.s04Ref: e.g. {"ref": "@q-lata", "kinds": ["question"], "data": {"form": "match", "prompt": "Match the year with the event", "left": ["1410", "1569", "1791", "1918"], "right": ["Battle of Grunwald", "Union of Lublin", "Constitution of 3 May", "Regaining independence"], "leftLabel": "Year", "rightLabel": "Event", "show": 3}}
body.s05Ref: e.g. {"ref": "@q-atom", "kinds": ["question"], "data": {"form": "one", "prompt": "What is in the nucleus of an atom?", "options": ["Electrons", "Protons and neutrons", "Only neutrons"], "correct": [1], "about": ["@atom"]}}
body.s06Ref: e.g. {"ref": "@q-orbital", "kinds": ["question"], "data": {"form": "truefalse", "prompt": "One orbital can hold at most two electrons.", "value": true, "about": ["@orbital"], "needs": ["@q-atom"]}}
body.s07Gap:
"gap" — [[word]] in the content is a gap (the learner sees “…”), and without "answers" the correct answer is that word; several gaps — each on its own (result: the share of correct gaps);
      "choices" — for each gap in turn a list of WRONG options: a gap with a list is chosen from (the correct word is added automatically, formulas allowed), one with an empty [] — typed
body.s08: FORMULAS: $…$ inline, $$…$$ on their own — in the question, options, pairs, items, tiles, hints, explanation; \$ is a plain dollar; typing an answer never requires LaTeX
body.s09Hints: "hints" — hints before answering (1–3, from gentle to specific): each one revealed lowers the highest score of this answer by 0.25 (one — at most 0.75);
body.s10Explanation:
"explanation" — explanation (markup, 2–4 sentences, formulas, sources [@dzieło, p. 12]) right after the answer, expanded; "explain" — entries after it, collapsed;
      story slides at the start of "explain" (entries of a kind with the field “Content in blocks”, shown by a flow’s "show" step) come FIRST after the answer, drawn as in the player (title, text, quotes with “> — Author”, formulas, footnotes), collapsed; under an expanded one: “See in the story” (a preview of the story at this slide: saves nothing; first a story already started, then a deeper one before the review, with the detour ladder “Stage 1 › The nine-year-old’s dream”) and “Questions on this slide (N)” with “Practise”; questions about the same starting slides are one map field “Questions” next to “Stories”; "explain" pointing to the UNIT of a story (“Part of the story”, when the question covers the whole story, e.g. a timeline) — the field “Whole story” of that story, and “See in the story” opens it from the start; do not put a [@klucz] citation into "prompt" (the import warns) — the source belongs in "explanation";
body.s11Feedback: "feedback" (one, many) — one sentence for each option, in the order of "options" ("" — no sentence): after the answer it stands under the chosen one and under the correct ones
body.s13Code: "code" — "tests": visible examples [{"input": …, "output": …, "note": "…"}] (JSON values or JSON text), checked before the hidden cases from "createInput"/"reference"; each case has 2 s; result: the share passed
body.s15: EXPRESSION LANGUAGE in generators (let, require, where, {…}, “Compute”):

question.head: question — ONE kind "question"; "form" (the question type) says how it is asked, and it decides which fields are filled in:

questionExample.right: ["Battle of Grunwald", "Union of Lublin", "Constitution of 3 May"]
questionExample.feedback: ["Too few — count the empty set too.", "", "Yes: 2^3 = 8.", "Too many."]

aiPrompt.entities: List the people, places, works and other things in the text as entries.
aiPrompt.statements: Split the text into statements — entries of a kind with a "blocks" field ({kinds}). Each begins with a thesis — one short sentence; then paragraphs, lists, tables; references to entries as {"ref": "@…", "locator": "…"} in cells or [[word|@ref]] in a paragraph.
aiPrompt.statementsMissing: this base does not have one yet: add to "kinds" {"ref": "@komentarz", "name": "Comment", "label": "{content}", "fields": [{"key": "about", "label": "About", "type": "ref", "multi": true, "locator": true}, {"key": "content", "label": "Content", "type": "blocks"}]}
aiPrompt.questions: Write questions from the text that check knowledge (one kind "question"), using different question types ("form": text, one, many, truefalse, match, order, gap, flash…) — pick the type that fits what you ask (dates and their events: "match" with "show"; a statement to judge: "truefalse"). First questions about general things, then specific ones: a question that requires knowing the answer to another has "needs": ["@that-one"]; "about" points to the entries the question checks.
aiPrompt.flow: Build a flow (format {flowFormat}): steps showing statements and questions; all texts are statements (entries with a "blocks" field), not text of the flow.
aiPrompt.schema: Propose kinds (kinds) with fields that describe such entries.
aiPrompt.answerOnly: Reply ONLY with a JSON document in the format "{format}" (version 1), without comments.
aiPrompt.useRefs: Use your own "ref" names (e.g. "@david") and refer to entries with them.

top.library: the knowledge base the answers come from: {"id", "name"} — the import refuses another base; omitted — import into the base open here
top.answers: answers (below), at most {max} in one import

library.name: name of the knowledge base (information only)

answer.id: identifier of the answer from the export — an answer already in your progress is skipped; without "id" the answer is new (unless there is already an answer to the same card "key" at the same moment "at")
answer.key: card: question and direction ("question|direction" or just the question) — required, up to {max} characters; only such a card of this base counts the answer
answer.question: the card’s question (the part of "key" before "|"); omitted — from "key"
answer.direction: the card’s direction (the part of "key" after "|", e.g. "a-b"); omitted — from "key"
answer.fingerprint: a fingerprint of what was the correct answer at the time — when the card’s content changes, old answers stop counting; omitted — the answer always counts
answer.at: when: ISO date and time ("2026-10-28T18:03:11Z") or milliseconds since 1970 — from 2020 until today
answer.correctness: how well: a number from 0 (wrong) to 1 (right), fractions for partly correct answers; true/false also
answer.ms: how long the answer took, in milliseconds (at most a day)
answer.given: what was given, briefly (up to {max} characters — longer is cut)
answer.via: where from: a revision, session or flow (e.g. "revision:<id>") — information only, for analysis
answer.hints: how many hints the learner revealed before answering (each lowers the highest score by 0.25) — information only
answer.params: a task from a generator: the drawn values, e.g. {"a": 37, "n": 5}, drawn entries as "@identifier", short lists ["…", "…"] — which version came up; information only
answer.seed: the draw number of a generator task — with it exactly the same task is created (the same values and entries); information only
answer.text: information only, from the export: what the card asked, in words — the import does not read it

usage.title: How the app uses this data

progress.title: My progress as JSON ("{format}", version {version})
progress.text:
Your answers in one knowledge base: to which card, how well, when, how long and what was given — to keep or to analyse (e.g. with AI: what is difficult, how answer times change). In the app: Learning → knowledge base → “Progress” → “My progress as JSON”, #/workspace/learn/<baza>/postepy.
What the import does:
- It first shows a plan; it saves only after “Import”.
- It adds answers only to YOUR progress in the base open here — never to anyone else’s (the document does not say whose they are: it is always the progress of the person importing). It rejects a document from another base ("library.id").
- It skips an answer whose "id" is already in your progress — the same export imported a second time changes nothing. An answer without "id" is new (unless there is already an answer to the same card at the same moment "at").
- It changes and deletes nothing: an answer has happened.
- It saves new answers as new batches of {perBatch}, sealed in the browser for you (and for the course’s intake area, if the base names one — leaders see them in “Learners’ progress”), like every answer from learning. Without internet they wait on this device.
- An answer to a card that does not exist in this base is saved with a warning — it counts only once such a card exists. An answer in the wrong shape — a warning, skipped.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.
